newsitem.title: USA: UAW-Ford workers ratify new labor contract.
newsitem.headline: UAW-Ford workers ratify new labor contract.

text.p: United Auto Workers members at Ford Motor Co. overwhelmingly approved a new three-year labour contract with the automaker that provides unprecedented employment guarantees, the union said Monday.
The UAW said Ford production workers who voted on the contract ratified it by a 90 percent margin. In a separate vote, UAW-Ford skilled trades workers approved the pact by an 83 percent margin.

The contract guarantees jobs for 95 percent of Ford's current UAW workforce of 105,000. The three-year agreement gives workers a $2,000 lump sum payment in the first year, followed by 3 percent base wage hikes in the second and third years.
Other items include higher pension benefits to those who retire during the contract, tuition assistance of up to $1,000 per year for eligible dependent children and Christmas bonuses of up to $600.
UAW President Stephen Yokich and Ernest Lofton, UAW vice president for Ford, attributed the high approval rate to the job security, wage gains and other benefits in the contract.
"We are delighted with the outstanding acceptance by Ford workers of the new agreement," they said in a statement.

The vote comes one day after the UAW and Chrysler Corp. reached a tentative agreement patterned after the economic terms in the Ford deal. Company and union officials would not release details of the agreement, but indicated that its major terms followed the pattern set by Ford.
UAW National Chrysler Council, made up of plant-level officers and bargainers, are scheduled to vote on the deal Thursday in Detroit.
